key_insight: The paper shows that for affine robust optimization, only a sparse subset of uncertainty directions may be needed, and these can be selected with provable coverage guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This enables more tractable robust ML and optimization pipelines by replacing large uncertainty sets with a smaller atomic set that still preserves key robustness behavior.
method: Model uncertainty as a finite dictionary with a budget constraint and select a subset of directions as an atomic uncertainty set.
Use a data-driven coverage objective over evaluation directions such as gradients, adversarial perturbations, or held-out data shifts.
Apply a greedy selection algorithm justified by monotone submodularity, with a (1-1/e) approximation guarantee and a loss certificate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, including a matching hardness barrier, plus out-of-sample control for radius calibration on held-out evaluation directions.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the chosen dictionary and evaluation directions, so poor coverage may miss important uncertainty modes.
paper_title: Which Directions Matter? Sparse Design for Affine Robust Optimization
